title: Sharpness and critical scaling of parking
summary: In the parking model, each site of the $d$-dimensional lattice independently starts with one car with probability $p$ or one parking spot with probability $1-p$. Cars move according to independent discrete-time simple random walks and park at the first spot they find free. We prove that in the critical regime $p=1/2$, the expected number of visits to a site in $n$ rounds is of order $n^{(4-d)/4}$ for $d\leq3$ and $\log n$ for $d\geq4$.
